Lunch rush, four consumers on a queue: a redelivery can change the order, and "out for delivery" arrives before "paid". In Kafka, the topic has partitions; events with the same key (the order id) always land in the same partition and are read in the order they were written. In a group, each partition has one consumer at a time: with three partitions, the fourth consumer sits idle.

What would the event key be in your system? Tell me in the comments.

Sources: Apache Kafka 4.4 and RabbitMQ (Queues) documentation. Part 3 of 4 of the Kafka series.

The author's voice is cloned with AI. Animations made for this video; fictional app, services and orders.
